components.Settings.SettingsGuide.flow1: Someone requests a title. It waits for an admin unless their permissions approve it on their own (Users).
components.Settings.SettingsGuide.flow2: Once approved it is sent to Radarr (movies) or Sonarr (series), which search the indexers through Prowlarr and hand what they pick to the download client: qBittorrent or SABnzbd.
components.Settings.SettingsGuide.flow3: When the download finishes, Radarr or Sonarr import it into the library folder, renamed their way.
components.Settings.SettingsGuide.flow4: A minute after an import, Seerr AI asks the media server (Plex, Jellyfin or Emby) what it has added, and again each minute a few times until it lists it. Otherwise the server is asked every 5 minutes, and the whole library is read at 3am.
components.Settings.SettingsGuide.flow5: Once the media server lists it, the title is Available and the requester is told, by web push or whatever they have turned on.

However many albums, it is one request, approved once. Approved, it goes to Lidarr, which monitors and searches for exactly those albums and nothing else of the artist’s.
components.Settings.SettingsGuide.music2: Music Sync (every 5 minutes, and a minute after Lidarr imports something) follows Lidarr’s work and reads what each media server’s music libraries have added; the Music Full Scan reads all of them at 3:40am. An album is Available once a music library lists it, or, with no music library switched on anywhere, once Lidarr has all its tracks. The requester is told when every album they asked for is here.

components.Settings.SettingsGuide.stuck1: Backfill (Settings → Backfill) looks every 6 hours for titles Radarr or Sonarr searched for and did not find. Approvals come as a Backfill notification; small, safe packs can be approved automatically.
components.Settings.SettingsGuide.stuck2: The admin agent (an AI, with AI set up) looks further when Backfill finds nothing usable: it reads why releases were turned down and searches other ways.
